=={{header|Cxc}}==

Cxc has no <code>while</code> loop; iteration folds into the atom lifecycle. The <code>main</code> atom enters <code>running</code> and self-sends <code>tick(n: 1)</code>. Each <code>tick</code> arm prints one line and self-sends <code>tick(n: n + 1)</code> until <code>n > 100</code> transitions the atom to <code>end</code>. The <code>|:</code> glyph marks guard arms on the same message, resolved first-match.

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
def main:
    -> running
        then: self :> tick(n: 1)

    running <: tick(n: Int!):
        |: n > 100 -> end
        |: n % 15 == 0 -> running
            then:
                print("FizzBuzz")
                self :> tick(n: n + 1)
        |: n % 3 == 0 -> running
            then:
                print("Fizz")
                self :> tick(n: n + 1)
        |: n % 5 == 0 -> running
            then:
                print("Buzz")
                self :> tick(n: n + 1)
        |: else -> running
            then:
                print(n.to_string())
                self :> tick(n: n + 1)

    -> end
</syntaxhighlight>

The <code>:></code> operator is an asynchronous self-send that enqueues the next <code>tick</code> on the atom's own serial dispatch queue; the arm body runs to completion before the next tick's guards are evaluated.
